subject: Clarify SOW language: no-model-learning vs. derivative license (HealthEdge)
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthedge.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthedge.com
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOW language — model improvement and derivative rights

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and procurement teams are working to finalize the SOW and purchase order. Attached is our SOW draft (HealthEdge_SOW_draft_v1.docx) — there are two items where we need explicit confirmation from Redwood before we can sign:

1) No-model-learning/no-training commitment: the draft currently says "Provider will not use Customer data to improve models." Can you confirm Redwood's operational verification steps and whether you are willing to include a short attestation that you will not train or fine-tune models on HealthEdge data?

2) Derivative rights / output ownership: we need clarity on whether outputs (prompts/responses) are considered Customer data with exclusive license to HealthEdge, or whether Redwood retains any derivative rights for model improvements or product analytics.

We also need a list of subprocessors and their residency (for export/control purposes) and a proof path (evidence pack) for no-training claims we can attach to our procurement file.

Can you share a proposed clause and an attestation template we can review? Preferably by EOD Tuesday — procurement is on a timeline.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Sr. Contracts Manager | HealthEdge
Attachment: HealthEdge_SOW_draft_v1.docx (DOCX, 56KB)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOW language — model improvement and derivative rights

David / Kim — forwarding HealthEdge's SOW draft and ask. Key asks: a short no-training attestation, subprocessor/residency list, and clarification on "derivative rights" vs "no-training".

Proposed immediate plan:
- Kim: can you produce a concise redline for the SOW clause that uses our standard "no-model-learning" wording but also clarifies derivative ownership (prompt/response entitlements)?
- David: ops to assemble a minimal evidence pack (subprocessor list with region, statement of KV/prefix cache behavior, and that we do not persist customer prompts for model training). We should avoid producing anything that looks like a full SOC report — a short operational summary should suffice for procurement.

Timeline: HealthEdge needs something by EOD Tuesday (2027-08-24 UTC). I will take point on coordinating the external reply.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — https://www.redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthedge.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW language — proposed redline and attestation template

Hi Maya — thanks for sharing the draft. Attached are two items:

1) RW_redline_no_learning_clause.docx — a suggested redline for the SOW that: 
   - Replaces ambiguous "use to improve models" language with a specific "no-model-learning" clause: 
     "Provider will not use Customer-provided data (including prompts, uploads, or other inputs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any foundation or production models used to serve Customer requests without Customer's explicit written consent."
   - Adds a definition for "Derivatives/Outputs": "Customer Outputs (prompts, responses, generated content) are Customer Data and Customer retains exclusive rights to use, export, and license such Outputs. Provider will not assert derivative rights over Outputs nor use Outputs to train models."

2) attestation_template.pdf — a signed attestation stub Redwood legal/ops can provide post-signature stating the operational controls and confirmation we will not use Customer data for model training.

A few clarifying notes / questions we have for you:
- When you say "derivative rights," do you mean Redwood shouldn't be able to reuse outputs for product analytics or internal model retraining? We treated "derivative" as both (a) intellectual property claims over outputs and (b) using outputs to improve models; the redline covers both.
- Please confirm whether HealthEdge requires subprocessors' encryption key residency details (KMS onshore/offshore) or just locations and data access roles.

Attachment: RW_redline_no_learning_clause.docx (DOCX, 12KB)
Attachment: attestation_template.pdf (PDF, 4KB)

Kimberly / Tessa — thanks for the fast turnaround, the redline looks good overall. A couple of small edits from procurement:

- In the attestation, we need an explicit sentence that confirms "we will not use Customer Outputs for internal product analytics that result in model parameter updates." The current attestation is fine but please add that line.
- Subprocessor details: procurement needs a CSV with subprocessor name, country, and whether they have access to plaintext customer prompts. Key-residency details (KMS) are optional for now but may be requested later.

I've attached the PO (Purchase_Order_HealthEdge_20270823.pdf). Once we have the signed attestation (template filled and signed) and the subprocessor CSV, procurement can route for signature. We can sign the SOW with your redline and the minor attestation edit. DocuSign link would be helpful.

Can we set a brief 30-min call on Wednesday to confirm outstanding evidence items? 11:30am PT works on our side.

Thanks,
